gaps.sentence: I ___ the car tonight, so take a taxi into town.
gaps.hint: a future activity in progress as reason
gaps.explanation: The future continuous can express something in progress around a future time, here as a polite reason: will be using.

gaps.sentence: At the moment, the council ___ whether to sell the library.
gaps.hint: at the moment shows an ongoing process
gaps.explanation: 'At the moment' marks an ongoing process, so the present continuous fits: is deciding.

gaps.sentence: This month they ___ a new wing to the hospital, so some services are elsewhere.
gaps.hint: this month means a temporary current period
gaps.explanation: 'This month' describes a temporary situation around now, so the present continuous fits: are adding.

gaps.sentence: He ___ very shy at first, but once you know him he is very chatty.
gaps.hint: seem describes a state not action
gaps.explanation: 'Seem' describes a state and is not used continuously: seems.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her laptop repaired twice this year already.
gaps.explanation: 'Has had it repaired twice this year' — present perfect of causative have.

gaps.sentence: Look at those clouds — it ___ any minute now.
gaps.explanation: A prediction based on present evidence uses 'be going to': is going to rain.

gaps.sentence: The conference ___ on Monday and ends on Wednesday.
gaps.explanation: Fixed schedules are stated in the present simple: starts.

gaps.sentence: The bus ___ at 6.40 tomorrow morning, according to the timetable.
gaps.hint: official timetables use the present simple
gaps.explanation: Official timetables take the present simple for future events: leaves.
